claims: C1 instructions with higher authority override those with lower authority
C2 the chain-of-command principle is designed to maximize steerability and control for users and developers

concepts.name: chain_of_command_principle
concepts.gloss: the principle that instructions with higher authority override those with lower authority, designed to maximize steerability and control

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: the ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts

concepts.name: instruction_authority_level
concepts.gloss: instruction I is assigned a level of authority L
concepts.inference: the clause says each instruction is assigned a level of authority, so a relation between an instruction and its level must exist

concepts.name: higher_authority
concepts.gloss: the authority level of instruction I is higher than the authority level of instruction J
concepts.inference: the clause compares authority levels to determine which instruction prevails, so a comparison relation is needed

ontology.gloss: P is the chain-of-command principle that instructions with higher authority override those with lower authority

asserts.read_back: instruction % overrides instruction % because % has higher authority than %
asserts.body: instruction_authority_level(I, LI), instruction_authority_level(J, LJ), higher_authority(I, J)

closure.reason: the clause states when an override occurs but does not forbid or permit any act; silence about other overrides leaves them permitted
